rows.label: Kabbalah
rows.description: esoteric discipline and school of thought, associated with Judaism
rows.hook: centres on mystical readings of sacred texts and a diagram called the Tree of Life

rows.label: Protestantism
rows.description: branch of Christianity that emerged following the Protestant Reformation of the 16th century in opposition to the Roman Catholic Church and rejects papal supremacy
rows.hook: arose when reformers broke away from the Catholic Church during the Reformation

rows.label: Lutheranism
rows.description: form of Protestantism commonly associated with the teachings of Martin Luther
rows.hook: follows the ideas of a German monk who famously posted 95 theses against church practices

rows.label: Pentecostalism
rows.hook: emphasises spiritual gifts such as speaking in tongues, inspired by a biblical festival day

rows.label: Mennonites
rows.description: Anabaptist groups originating in Western Europe
rows.hook: are known for pacifist beliefs and a plain, community-centred way of life

rows.label: Anglicanism
rows.description: Christian tradition developing out of the practices, liturgy and identity of the Church of England
rows.hook: grew out of the national church of England after a king broke with the pope

rows.label: Evangelicalism
rows.hook: stresses personal conversion, being born again, and the authority of the Bible

rows.label: Presbyterianism
rows.description: branch of Protestant Christianity using presbyterian church government and originating in the British Isles
rows.hook: is governed by elected elders rather than bishops and traces back to John Knox in Scotland

rows.label: Methodism
rows.description: group of historically related denominations of Protestant Christianity
rows.hook: began as a movement led by John Wesley and is named for its methodical approach to devotion

rows.label: Anabaptism
rows.hook: rejected infant baptism in the sixteenth century, insisting on a believer's own choice

rows.label: Baptists
rows.hook: practise full-immersion baptism of believers and prize the independence of each congregation

rows.label: Zen
rows.hook: stresses seated meditation and puzzling riddles called koans

rows.label: Eastern Orthodoxy
rows.hook: split from the Western church in the Great Schism and is led by patriarchs such as the one in Constantinople

rows.label: Oriental Orthodox churches
rows.description: largest group of churches following Oriental Orthodoxy in full communion
rows.hook: includes the Coptic, Armenian and Ethiopian communions, which separated after a fifth-century council

rows.label: Vaishnavism
rows.description: major Hindu tradition that reveres Vishnu as the Supreme Being
rows.hook: venerates the preserver deity, whose avatars include Rama and Krishna

rows.label: Mahāyāna
rows.description: branch of Buddhism popular in East Asia and Vietnam that sees the goal of becoming a buddha through the bodhisattva path as being available to all and sees the state of the arhat as incomplete
rows.hook: teaches the ideal of the bodhisattva, who vows to help every being reach enlightenment

rows.label: Theravāda
rows.description: major branch of Buddhism following the Pāli Canon, dominant in Sri Lanka, Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and Thailand
rows.hook: is the dominant tradition in Sri Lanka and Thailand and follows scriptures written in Pali
